report.tagline: A UK digital bank that started as the world's first person-to-person lending site and now offers loans, car finance, credit cards, savings and a current account.
report.simpleSummary: Zopa is an app bank in the UK. It is best known for personal loans and car finance, with a quick decision and fair rates for people with good credit. It pays good interest on savings, and since 2025 it also has a current account called Biscuit. It started in 2005 as a website where ordinary people lent money to each other, then turned itself into a full bank.

overview.whatItDoes: Zopa lends money to UK consumers through personal loans, car finance and credit cards, and funds those loans with savings deposits. It decides who to lend to with its own credit models. It added a current account in 2025 to become people's everyday bank.
howItWorks: You check your loan rate in the app or on a comparison site without hurting your credit score (a soft search).
Zopa's model looks at your credit file, income and bank data and gives a personal rate in minutes.
If you accept, money usually lands the same day, and you repay monthly by direct debit.
Savers put money in fixed-term or easy-access accounts and ISAs, protected up to £85,000 by FSCS.
Zopa earns the gap between what borrowers pay and what savers earn, minus losses on bad loans.
The Biscuit current account adds everyday spending, salary and Boosted savings pots.
overview.valueProposition: Fair, fast credit with a price based on your real risk, and good savings rates, from a bank built only for the app.

businessModel.summary: Zopa makes money by lending. It pays savers interest, lends that money at higher rates, and keeps the difference after losses. The current account adds cheaper deposits and better data for lending.

revenueStreams.detail: The biggest stream. Rates depend on borrower risk.
Interest on balances not paid in full, and interchange on card spend.
Interchange, a small fee the shop's bank pays when you use the card, plus cheaper deposits.

businessModel.pricing: Personal loan representative APR varies by amount and term, typically in the mid to high single digits for larger loans, higher for small ones. Savings rates change often. Current account is free. See zopa.com for current rates.
costDrivers: Credit losses on loans that are not repaid
Marketing and fees paid to comparison sites and car dealers
Provisions for the UK motor finance commission review (£7.9 million in 2025)
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take an £8,000 loan at about 9% interest. Zopa earns roughly £720 in interest in the first year. It pays about 4% to savers to fund it, about £320. It expects to lose perhaps 2% to 3% of the loan to defaults, about £200. It pays maybe £100 to £150 to the comparison site that sent the customer. That leaves a small profit of about £50 to £100 in year one, more if the customer takes a second product. This is why good credit models matter: a 1% change in losses can wipe out the profit.

howTheyGetUsers: Comparison sites like ClearScore, MoneySuperMarket and Experian
Cross-selling: savers get loan offers and borrowers get savings offers
Partnerships such as embedded finance with retailers
whatBringsUsersBack: Monthly loan repayments in the app
Repeat borrowing with better rates for good payers
Biscuit current account for everyday use
growth.moat: Twenty years of repayment data and credit models tuned to UK borrowers, plus a full bank licence that gives it cheap deposits. Rivals can copy the app, but not the data or the risk know-how quickly.

competitors.name: Monzo
competitors.positioning: Big app bank adding loans and savings to a large current account base.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Zopa started with lending and is adding a current account; Monzo started with the account and is adding lending.

competitors.name: Starling Bank
competitors.positioning: App bank strong with small businesses.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Zopa is mainly a consumer lender; Starling is mainly an everyday account bank.

competitors.name: Big banks (Lloyds, Barclays, NatWest)
competitors.positioning: Full range of products, branches and huge customer bases.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Zopa is quicker and often cheaper on loans, but has fewer products.

competitors.name: Chase UK
competitors.positioning: JPMorgan's UK app bank with strong savings and cashback.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Zopa has deep lending history; Chase UK has deep pockets.

competitors.name: Funding Circle
competitors.positioning: Another former person-to-person lender, focused on small business loans.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Zopa became a bank; Funding Circle stayed a lending platform.

northStar.metric: Number of customers with an active Zopa product who are repaying or saving successfully
northStar.why: It shows customers getting value, either credit they can afford or savings growing, and it ties directly to Zopa's profit. Counting new loans alone could reward risky lending. That is what makes it a good north star metric: it moves only when customers get real value.

pmLessons: In lending, the risk model is the product. The app gets customers in, but the model decides profit.
Pivoting from a marketplace to a bank traded growth speed for cheaper, steadier funding.
Adding a daily-use product like a current account can improve the core business through better data.
Win one product first, then cross-sell.

interviewQuestions.question: Zopa launched a current account. How would you measure if it is working?
interviewQuestions.hint: Define success: main accounts, deposits, cross-sell, cost. Pick a north star like salary-funded accounts. Guardrails: fraud, complaints.

interviewQuestions.question: Why did Zopa stop being a person-to-person lending platform?
interviewQuestions.hint: Explain funding: retail lenders pull money in crises, banks have stable deposits and FSCS. Talk about regulation and trust.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow loans without raising defaults?
interviewQuestions.hint: Better data (open banking), better targeting, repeat customers, price for risk. Track approval rate and default rate together.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a product for credit builders.
interviewQuestions.hint: Persona: thin file. Low-limit card, education, rewards for on-time payment. Metric: score improvement and on-time rate.

interviewQuestions.question: A rival offers 1% better savings rates. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Check how rate-sensitive your savers are, the cost of matching, and other ways to retain like pots and ISAs. Model the trade-off.
